newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian Co-Premier rejects poll alliance offer.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian Co-Premier rejects poll alliance offer.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen on Friday rejected an offer to join an alliance headed by his main rival in the coalition government.
But he said his Cambodian People's Party wanted to continue working with the royalist FUNCINPEC party of First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh in government and parliament.

"The CPP cannot join with any front because we are the CPP, a big party, and we cannot accept to join with any front, but we can cooperate with any party," Hun Sen told reporters attending the opening day of the annual CPP congress.
"We continue with FUNCINPEC in government, in the national assembly, and we want to cooperate for the future," he added.

Ranariddh on Thursday confirmed plans to form a new political alliance, including Khmer Rouge defectors and the unrecognised opposition Khmer Nation Party, for elections due in 1998. He said the CPP could join if it wanted.

FUNCINPEC and the formerly communist CPP formed an alliance after U.N.-run elections in 1993. But uneasy relations have been strained in the past year by the royalists' demand for a greater share of power, and by the two parties rival efforts to win the allegiance of thousands of Khmer Rouge defectors in recent months.
